distractors.reason: 'Fellow' means a colleague or a member of the same group. We don't say 'fellow review' for the evaluation of academic work.
'Mutual' means shared by two parties. It does not form the established term 'review' for academic evaluation.
'Guest' describes a visiting person, not an evaluation process. 'Guest review' is not an established academic collocation.

example_sentence: The article was accepted only after a rigorous ___ review by two independent referees.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes suelen invertir el orden o añadir una preposición, diciendo 'review of peers' o 'review by peers'. En inglés el sustantivo modificador va delante del núcleo: 'peer review'.
explanation: In English compound nouns, the first noun works as a modifier and comes before the head noun, as in 'peer review', 'exam paper' or 'bus stop'. The reversed order does not form the established term.

related_collocations.example: Before starting the project, she wrote a literature review.
The research design determines how the data will be collected.
The data set was cleaned before the statistical analysis.

memory_tip: PEER REVIEW = evaluation by equals (peers) | the modifier goes FIRST, the head noun LAST
